The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

_pdu() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd

        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="pdu"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        pdu)
            opts="-b -H -q -d -w -m -s -p -h -V --json-input --json-output --bytes-format --detect-links --dedupe-links --deduplicate-hardlinks --top-down --align-right --quantity --depth --max-depth --width --total-width --column-width --min-ratio --no-sort --no-errors --silent-errors --progress --threads --omit-json-shared-details --omit-json-shared-summary --help --version [FILES]..."
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --bytes-format)

                    ;;

                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))

                    ;;
                -w)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))

                    ;;
                --column-width)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))

/// Fit a node and its descendants into the column, dropping what does not fit.
fn fit(node: &DataTree, depth: usize, max_width: usize, widest: &mut usize) -> Option<FittedNode> {
    let children: Vec<FittedNode> = node
        .children
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|child| fit(child, depth + 1, max_width, widest))
        .collect();
    let indent = depth * INDENT_WIDTH;
    let name = display_name(&node.name);
    let full_width = indent + BRANCH_WIDTH + display_width(&name);
    let mut fitted = FittedNode {
        name,
        size: node.size,
        width: full_width,
        children,
    };
    if full_width > max_width {
        let name_max = max_width.checked_sub(indent + BRANCH_WIDTH)?;
        let new_len = name_max.checked_sub(ELLIPSIS.len())?;
        if new_len == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        fitted.shorten_name(new_len);
        fitted.width = indent + BRANCH_WIDTH + display_width(&fitted.name);
    }
    *widest = (*widest).max(fitted.width);
    Some(fitted)
}

impl FittedNode {
    /// Shorten the name to `new_len` bytes and mark it as truncated.
    fn shorten_name(&mut self, new_len: usize) {
        self.name.truncate(new_len);
        self.name.push_str(ELLIPSIS);
    }
}

struct WithDecimalPoint(f64);

impl Display for WithDecimalPoint {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        struct LookForDecimalPoint<'f, 'a> {
            formatter: &'f mut fmt::Formatter<'a>,
            has_decimal_point: bool,
        }

        impl<'f, 'a> fmt::Write for LookForDecimalPoint<'f, 'a> {
            fn write_str(&mut self, fragment: &str) -> fmt::Result {
                self.has_decimal_point |= fragment.contains('.');
                self.formatter.write_str(fragment)
            }

            fn write_char(&mut self, ch: char) -> fmt::Result {
                self.has_decimal_point |= ch == '.';
                self.formatter.write_char(ch)
            }
        }

        if self.0.is_finite() {
            let mut writer = LookForDecimalPoint {
                formatter,
                has_decimal_point: false,
            };
            tri!(write!(writer, "{}", self.0));
            if !writer.has_decimal_point {
                tri!(formatter.write_str(".0"));
            }
        } else {
            tri!(write!(formatter, "{}", self.0));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

    name: String,

    /// Whether the node was the last of its siblings before anything was dropped.

/// Fit a node and its descendants into the column, dropping what does not fit.
/// Dropped descendants that would fit on their own still count towards `widest`.
fn fit(
    node: &DataTree,
    depth: usize,
    last_in_full_tree: bool,
    max_width: usize,
    widest: &mut usize,
) -> Option<FittedNode> {
    let count = node.children.len();
    let children: Vec<FittedNode> = node
        .children
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter_map(|(index, child)| fit(child, depth + 1, index + 1 == count, max_width, widest))
        .collect();
    let indent = depth * INDENT_WIDTH;
    let name = display_name(&node.name);
    let full_width = indent + BRANCH_WIDTH + display_width(&name);
    let size = node.size;
    let mut fitted = FittedNode { name, size, width: full_width, last_in_full_tree, children };
    if full_width > max_width {
        let name_max = max_width.checked_sub(indent + BRANCH_WIDTH)?;
        let new_len = name_max.checked_sub(ELLIPSIS.len())?;
        if new_len == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        fitted.shorten_name(new_len);
        fitted.width = indent + BRANCH_WIDTH + display_width(&fitted.name);
    }
    *widest = (*widest).max(fitted.width);
    Some(fitted)
}

    fn shorten_name(&mut self, new_len: usize) {
        self.name.truncate(new_len);
        self.name.push_str(ELLIPSIS);
    }

//! Sub-routines of the application.

use super::{overlapping_arguments::remove_overlapping_dirs, terminal, RuntimeError};
use crate::{
    args::{Args, ColumnWidth},
    bytes_format::BytesFormat,
    data_tree::DataTree,
    hardlink::{hardlink_list::SharedInfo, HardlinkList, SharedSummary},
    json_data::{JsonBody, JsonData, JsonShared, SchemaVersion, Unit, UnitAndTree},
    reporter::{ErrorOnlyReporter, ProgressAndErrorReporter, Reporter},
    tree_builder::FsTreeBuilder,
    visualizer::{bar::BarAlignment, column_width::ColumnWidthDistribution, Direction, Visualizer},
};
use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::ffi::OsString;

/// Name of the virtual root that groups multiple arguments.
const TOTAL_NAME: &str = "(total)";
/// Version of the program as written in the JSON output.
const PDU_VERSION: &str = "0.21.1";

/// Decide how wide the chart should be.
fn column_width_distribution(column_width: Option<ColumnWidth>) -> ColumnWidthDistribution {
    match column_width {
        Some(ColumnWidth::Total(width)) => ColumnWidthDistribution::Total { width },
        Some(ColumnWidth::Components { tree, bar }) => ColumnWidthDistribution::Components {
            tree_width: tree,
            bar_width: bar,
        },
        None => ColumnWidthDistribution::Total {
            width: terminal::width().unwrap_or(terminal::DEFAULT_WIDTH),
        },
    }
}

/// Draw the chart and write it to stdout.
fn print_chart(args: &Args, tree: &DataTree, bytes_format: Option<BytesFormat>) {
    let visualizer = Visualizer {
        tree,
        bytes_format,
        direction: if args.top_down {
            Direction::TopDown
        } else {
            Direction::BottomUp
        },
        bar_alignment: if args.align_right {
            BarAlignment::Right
        } else {
            BarAlignment::Left
        },
        column_width: column_width_distribution(args.column_width),
    };

    let chart = visualizer.render();
    let stdout = io::stdout();
    let mut stdout = stdout.lock();
    for line in chart.split_inclusive('\n') {
        if stdout.write_all(line.as_bytes()).is_err() {
            print!("{line}");
        }
    }
    let _ = stdout.flush();
}

/// Build the trees of the arguments with the given reporter.
fn build_trees(
    args: &Args,
    files: &[PathBuf],
    reporter: &dyn Reporter,
    hardlinks: Option<&HardlinkList>,
) -> Vec<DataTree> {
    let builder = FsTreeBuilder {
        quantity: args.quantity,
        reporter,
        hardlinks,
    };
    files
        .iter()
        .map(|file| builder.build(file.clone(), OsString::from(file.as_os_str())))
        .collect()
}

/// Scan the filesystem and visualize the result.
pub fn filesystem(args: Args) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let mut files: Vec<PathBuf> = if args.files.is_empty() {
        vec![PathBuf::from(".")]
    } else {
        args.files.clone()
    };
    if args.deduplicate_hardlinks {
        files = remove_overlapping_dirs(files);
    }

    let hardlink_list = args.deduplicate_hardlinks.then(HardlinkList::new);
    let trees = if args.progress {
        let reporter = ProgressAndErrorReporter::new(args.silent_errors);
        let trees = build_trees(&args, &files, &reporter, hardlink_list.as_ref());
        reporter.finish();
        trees
    } else {
        let reporter = ErrorOnlyReporter { silent: args.silent_errors };
        let trees = build_trees(&args, &files, &reporter, hardlink_list.as_ref());
        reporter.finish();
        trees
    };

    let (mut tree, root_path): (DataTree, Option<&Path>) = match <[DataTree; 1]>::try_from(trees) {
        Ok([tree]) => (tree, Some(files[0].as_path())),
        Err(trees) => (DataTree::dir(OsString::from(TOTAL_NAME), 0, trees), None),
    };

    if !args.no_sort {
        tree.sort_by_size_desc();
    }
    tree.retain_min_ratio(args.min_ratio.get());
    tree.cut_depth(args.max_depth.as_u64());

    let shared = hardlink_list.map(|list| SharedInfo { records: list.into_records() });
    if let Some(shared) = &shared {
        shared.deduplicate(&mut tree, root_path);
    }

    let bytes_format = args.quantity.is_bytes().then_some(args.bytes_format);
    if args.json_output {
        return print_json(&args, tree, shared);
    }
    print_chart(&args, &tree, bytes_format);
    if let Some(shared) = shared {
        if !shared.is_empty() {
            print!("{}", shared.summary().display(bytes_format));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Serialize the tree and write it to stdout.
///
/// Names that are not valid UTF-8 cannot be represented in JSON.
fn print_json(args: &Args, tree: DataTree, shared: Option<SharedInfo>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let unit = if args.quantity.is_bytes() { Unit::Bytes } else { Unit::Blocks };
    let shared = shared.filter(|shared| !shared.is_empty()).map(|shared| JsonShared {
        details: (!args.omit_json_shared_details).then(|| shared.details()),
        summary: (!args.omit_json_shared_summary).then(|| shared.summary()),
    });
    let shared = shared.filter(|shared| !shared.is_empty());
    let body = JsonBody {
        unit_and_tree: UnitAndTree::new(
            unit,
            tree.into_reflection()
                .expect("convert all names from raw string to UTF-8"),
        ),
        shared,
    };
    let data = JsonData {
        schema_version: SchemaVersion,
        pdu: Some(PDU_VERSION.to_string()),
        body,
    };
    let text = serde_json::to_string(&data).map_err(RuntimeError::SerializationFailure)?;
    let stdout = io::stdout();
    let mut stdout = stdout.lock();
    // Failing to write (e.g. a closed pipe) is not considered an error.
    let _ = stdout.write_all(text.as_bytes());
    let _ = stdout.flush();
    Ok(())
}

/// Visualize a tree that was read from stdin as JSON.
pub fn json_input(args: Args) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if !args.files.is_empty() {
        return Err(RuntimeError::JsonInputArgConflict);
    }
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let data: JsonData = serde_json::from_reader(stdin.lock())
        .map_err(RuntimeError::DeserializationFailure)?;
    let unit = data.body.unit_and_tree.unit();
    let bytes_format = match unit {
        Unit::Bytes => Some(args.bytes_format),
        Unit::Blocks => None,
    };
    let JsonBody { unit_and_tree, shared } = data.body;
    let tree = unit_and_tree
        .into_tree()
        .into_data_tree(unit == Unit::Bytes)
        .map_err(RuntimeError::InvalidInputReflection)?;
    print_chart(&args, &tree, bytes_format);
    let summary = shared.and_then(|shared| match shared {
        JsonShared { summary: Some(summary), .. } => Some(summary),
        JsonShared { details: Some(details), .. } => {
            let records: Vec<_> = details.into_iter().map(|detail| detail.into_record()).collect();
            Some(SharedSummary::from_records(&records))
        }
        JsonShared { details: None, summary: None } => None,
    });
    if let Some(summary) = summary {
        println!("{}", summary.display(bytes_format));
    }
    Ok(())
}
</output>
